solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heartless barbs about American head coach expected here

indicators.note: a thing without a heart has lost its middle, so the central letters go
about means around, so one piece wraps itself round another

blocks.note: the word with its middle letters removed keeps only its ends
US is the standard abbreviation for American
the head of something is its top

explanation.surface: A sports coach is greeted with barbed insults from the stands.
explanation.walkthrough: B(US)S + TOP. 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer, but here it is a long-distance bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a large passenger road vehicle, and a stop is where waiting passengers board it.

clue.text: Bishop sitting on freezing cold, empty locomotive vehicle

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving just the outside pair of letters

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
freezing weather is icy
C is cold, as on a tap
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bishop sits in an unheated, deserted railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sitting on' puts the bishop above the rest. 'Locomotive vehicle' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'vehicle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle is a two-wheeled pedal-powered means of transport, an example of a vehicle.

clue.text: Gratis telly from Spooner that gives a hazy picture

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: gratis means without charge
a television is a TV set
swap the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: Free television from Spooner comes with a fuzzy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: FREE SET with its opening sounds exchanged becomes SEA FRET. 'Hazy picture' suggests bad reception, but the haze is real weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold coastal mist drifting in from the North Sea, which blurs the view.

clue.text: River water finally penetrating shelter

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
to penetrate is to get inside something, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: last letter of the word
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Rising river water eventually seeps into a camping shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: T(R)ENT. The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a long English waterway flowing through Nottingham to the Humber estuary.

clue.text: Reform/UKIP sect infiltrated by Left – most daring!

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
something infiltrated has an intruder slipped inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political headline: the Reform and UKIP faction has been infiltrated by left-wingers, and isn't that bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' looks like the name of the UK party Reform UK, as UKIP is another right-wing party, but it is the anagram signal; L goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means brave or spirited, so the superlative describes whoever shows the greatest courage.

clue.text: Cup specialists put Joey in the side

indicators.note: put ... in tells us to place one piece inside another

blocks.note: a joey is a young kangaroo, a roo for short
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A football club's cup specialists pick a player called Joey for the side.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA(ROO)M. 'Cup specialists' sounds like a team good in knockout competitions, but the cups are for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A café serving tea in cups and saucers is a place that specialises in that drink.

clue.text: Keep wicket during tense over

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one piece goes within the rest

blocks.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
o'er is the poetic contraction of over

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: keep wicket during a nervy over.
explanation.walkthrough: T + O(W)ER, using O'ER for over. 'Keep wicket' reads as the wicketkeeper's job; 'Keep' alone is the castle stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central stronghold of a castle, typically a tall tower.

clue.text: Each lav at work fitted with an ice-cold shower

indicators.note: things at work are being operated and moved about, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Every toilet at the office has been fitted with a freezing shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The bathroom setting makes 'shower' look like plumbing; it is a falling mass of snow and ice. Lav is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fall of snow and ice down a mountainside is, figuratively, a freezing downpour from above.

clue.text: Runs into dismissed policeman, one with stony face

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: a dismissed batsman is out
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a sacked police officer who keeps a stony expression.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT + C(R)OP. 'Stony face' suggests an expressionless person, but it is a literal rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is bedrock showing at the surface, so it presents an exposed rock face.

clue.text: Spring exam relating to civic office

blocks.note: May is a spring month
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A spring examination is held concerning a town hall post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like a verb or a coil, but here it is the season giving a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor holds the chief post in a town or city council, so mayoral concerns that municipal role.

clue.text: Nice big house?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pleasant, spacious home
setter's reading: a large residence in Nice, the French Riviera city, so called by its French name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of a clue hides its capital letter; the French city asks for the French word for a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word names a castle or stately country mansion, the kind of grand residence found around Nice.

clue.text: Wife, unrefined, left for Republican rolling in dough

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means it is swapped out and replaced

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
earthy humour is coarse and unrefined
L is left
R is Republican

explanation.surface: A coarse wife ditches the Republicans for the left and is making a fortune baking.
explanation.walkthrough: W + EARTHY with its R replaced by L. 'Dough' looks like baking but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling in it is an idiom for having heaps of money, and dough is slang for cash.

clue.text: Picture Kate racing back to catch janitor

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left
to catch is to hold, so the clue words hold the letters inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Imagine Kate sprinting back to catch the school janitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pictuRE KATE RACing' backwards. 'Picture' looks like a verb asking us to imagine, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Janitor is the American word for the person who looks after a building, called a caretaker in Britain.

clue.text: Weather better, though not fine – this’ll help dry clothes

indicators.note: saying 'but not' removes something from what came before

blocks.note: fairer weather is better weather
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A forecast: better weather but not fine, so a rack will help the washing dry.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIRER without its F. An airer is a British clothes-drying rack or clothes horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a folding frame on which damp laundry is hung to finish drying indoors.

clue.text: Give high praise to old flame returning fortune

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
your lot is your fate or fortune

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of a former lover who has come back with a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: EX + LOT backwards. 'Fortune' looks like wealth, but here it means one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol someone is to laud them enthusiastically, which is to praise them highly.

clue.text: Nepal lad shivering on river – he should be used to the cold

definitions.text: he should be used to the cold

indicators.note: something shivering is shaking about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boy from Nepal shivers beside a river, though he ought to be accustomed to the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Himalayan boy seems the cold-hardy one, but the definition points to the far north of Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Lapland lives within the Arctic Circle, so freezing winters are normal for such a person.

clue.text: Relative to see English spirit mate

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
pisco is a South American grape brandy
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: A family member goes to visit an English friend's ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like a family member and 'see' like looking, but a see is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's area of authority, and episcopal means pertaining to bishops.

clue.text: Wise Men never carrying incense upfront – it’s not true

indicators.note: upfront means at the very front, so only the opening letter counts and it leads

blocks.note: first letter of the word
the Magi are the Wise Men of the Nativity
nary is dialect for never or not one

explanation.surface: Doubting the Nativity story: the Wise Men never really brought incense.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi famously brought frankincense, so the surface reads as a sceptic's remark about the gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in the mind, so it is fictional rather than real.

clue.text: Queen dashed to palace to receive king

indicators.note: something dashed is smashed to pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently
receiving something takes it in, so one piece is held inside the others

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The queen hurried to the palace to greet the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed' reads as hurried, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, a famous historical female monarch.

clue.text: Tedious work penning a principally long, slow tune

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in, as in a pen
principally means chiefly, pointing to the chief or leading letter

blocks.note: a chore is a tedious task
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Writing a long, slow piece of music is a tedious job.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOR(A L)E. 'Penning' looks like composing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn melody, as in Lutheran church music, typically sung at a measured pace.

clue.text: Maintenance corps overturned a large diameter stone

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, which in a down entry means the letters run backwards

blocks.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, the British Army's maintenance corps
taken as written
L is the size abbreviation for large
D is the mathematical symbol for diameter

explanation.surface: Army engineers have tipped over a huge round boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large diameter stone' suggests a big rock; the definition is just the gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious gem, and stone is the usual jewellers' word for a gem.

clue.text: Spirit shown by those cycling?

indicators.note: cycling means going round and round, so letters move from the front to the back in turn

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Team spirit is on display among the cyclists.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the last letter of THOSE round to the front. The question mark flags that 'cycling' is not about bikes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic outlook or guiding character of a group, its prevailing spirit.

clue.text: Musical scrapped – it means a loss for bondholders

blocks.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
something scrapped has been cut

explanation.surface: A cancelled stage show costs its investors money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a flop show losing its backers' cash, which neatly matches the financial definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In finance a haircut is a reduction in the value creditors recover, a forced write-down on debt.

clue.text: One responsible for cuts in the workplace?

definitions.text: One responsible for cuts in the workplace?

blocks.clueFragment: One responsible for cuts in the workplace?
blocks.note: surface reading: a manager who axes jobs or budgets at work

blocks.clueFragment: One responsible for cuts in the workplace?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a doctor who makes incisions, whose workplace is the operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' suggests redundancies and spending cuts, but these are cuts with a scalpel.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical specialist operates by making incisions in patients in a hospital theatre.

clue.text: Ball game organised, the last in a series

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new arrangement

blocks.note: O is round like a ball
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A ball game is arranged as the final fixture of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: O + anagram of GAME. The surface sounds like a sports fixture list.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence used for the end of anything.

clue.text: US prison, I read, breaks senior officer

indicators.note: something that breaks falls apart and its letters can be put back differently

blocks.note: a brig is a military prison, an American term
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report: an American jail breaks a high-ranking officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' looks like a verb acting on the officer, but it signals the rearrangement of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is an army rank above colonel, commanding a brigade, so a high-ranking military commander.

clue.text: Chuck out case of Glenmorangie bottles drained during this?

indicators.note: a case is the outer covering, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: to bin something is to throw it away
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Throw out the empty bottles of a whole case of Scotch emptied in one sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a crate of whisky; it only frames the word. Glenmorangie is a Highland malt whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking spree in which large quantities of alcohol are consumed would empty many bottles.

clue.text: Opposed to Conservative buffoon from the past

blocks.note: anti means against
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political jibe: someone against the Tories calls a former leader a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural antics is familiar; the singular noun for a clown is archaic, hence 'from the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespearean English an antic was a grotesque performer or jester, an obsolete sense now.

clue.text: Boy given light salad dinner-time wraps

indicators.note: to wrap is to enclose, so the clue words enclose the letters

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A boy is served a light salad and some sandwich wraps at dinner time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like it describes the meal, but it belongs with 'Boy': the lad given a magic lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the youth Aladdin is handed a magic lamp, which gives light.

clue.text: Gold digit framing copper script on screen

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a toe is a digit of the foot
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Gold and copper metals sound like a TV crime drama script.
explanation.walkthrough: AU + TO(CU)E. Autocue is the British trade name for a teleprompter.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleprompter shows a presenter the words to read, scrolling on a monitor in front of the camera.

clue.text: Back loser, as Cockney might say

indicators.note: Cockneys famously drop the H, so we hear the words as spoken in that accent

blocks.note: the losing runner in a race is the horse at the end, said without its H

explanation.surface: Backing a horse that loses, in a Londoner's phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'loser' both suggest betting on horses, which is exactly where the wordplay goes; Cockney is the East London accent that drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal or candidate is to support or approve it publicly.

clue.text: By gum! Coal train regularly derailed here in Mexico

indicators.note: at even intervals letters are knocked off the track, so every other one is dropped and the rest kept

blocks.note: the even-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A startled exclamation as a coal train comes off the rails in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on. 'By gum!' is a mild northern English exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatán is a peninsula and state in south-east Mexico, so it is a place located there.
